utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon everybody. Would the Registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Case number IT-03-68-I, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. May I ask for the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Good afternoon, counsel. For the Prosecution appear Ms. Marie Tuma, trial attorney; Ms. Kimberly Fleming, trial support; and I Ekkehard Withopf, acting senior trial attorney.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Vasvega Vidovic, I'm Defence counsel for Mr. Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Ms. Vidovic. Mr. Oric, will you please stand up. Do you hear the proceedings in a language you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do, and I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For the record and identification, would you please state your full name.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you please also state your father and mother's name.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My father's name is Dzemal and my mother's name Hata.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. And what are the date and place of your birth?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 3rd of March, 1967, the village of Potocari, municipality of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The indictment against the accused Mr. Oric was reviewed and confirmed by another permanent Judge of this Tribunal on the 28th of March, 2003, with the arrest warrant issued on the same day. The accused was arrested on 10th of April, 2003, in Tuzla, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and transferred to the Detention Unit of this Tribunal on the next day. Upon the transfer of the accused, the President of the Tribunal assigned this case to Trial Chamber III and, as one of its judges, I have been designated as the Pre-Trial Judge. Today's proceeding is the initial appearance of the accused, pursuant to Rule 62 of our Rules of Procedure and Evidence. The first thing I have to do is to satisfy myself that the accused understands the indictment. Ms. Vidovic, did the accused receive the indictment?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, he received the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In a language he can understand?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In a language he understands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. It is the right of the accused to have the indictment read out in full in a language he speaks and understands. Ms. Vidovic, does your client wish to have the indictment read out?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: My client understood the indictment and he understood the indictment and he confirms it is not necessary to read it today again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Then the next step is then -- is a plea to the charges of the indictment. The accused may enter a plea within 30 days of the initial appearance, but he may plead -- he may enter a plea today if he so wishes. Ms. Vidovic, what is your client's intention? Does your client wish to enter a plea today or do it later?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: He wants to plea today. To plead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Oric, I will ask the Madam Registrar to put each count of the indictment to you. Then please enter your plea to each count and please confine your answer to either "guilty" or "not guilty." Madam Registrar, could you put each count to the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Count 1: Murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal and recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, how do you plead to that count 1?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And count 2, please. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 2: Cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Articles 3 and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal and recognised by Article 3(1)(a) of the Geneva Conventions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How do you plead to count 2, Mr. Oric?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, sirs, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. And count 3.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 3: Wanton destruction of cities, towns or villages, not justified by military necessity, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Articles 3(b) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. How do you plead to count 3?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, sirs, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Count 4.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 4: Plunder of public or private property, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Articles 3(e) and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Oric, how would you plead to that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, sirs, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And our final count.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I was mistaken -- yes, count 5.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 5: Wanton destruction of cities, towns or villages, not justified by military necessity, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Articles 3(b) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Oric, what is your plea to count 5?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, sirs, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. And count 6, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 6: Plunder of public or private property, a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Articles 3(e) and 7(1) of the Statute of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Oric, what is your plea?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, sirs, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. You may sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well, this concludes the first part, major part of our today's proceeding. Then I must now remind the Prosecution that pursuant to Rule 60(A)(i), to make available within 30 days to the Defence in a language that the accused understands all the supporting material which accompanied the indictment when the confirmation has been sought. Also, all prior statements obtained by the Prosecution from the accused must be disclosed as well. And also, let me now turn to the Defence and also tell the Defence that it will have a 30-day period for filing any preliminary motions that it may care to do, once it has received all the supporting materials, in accordance with Rule 66 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Having said that, I'd like to ask the parties whether there is -- there are any matters they wish to raise at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honour, from the side of the Prosecution, there is no further observation to be made. The Prosecution is well aware of its disclosure obligations and will comply with the Rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we have nothing to say now. We have no question to raise now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Oric, is there anything you would like to raise at this moment, in particular in regarding your arrest or anything else?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, sirs, I don't have anything to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Please sit down. According to Rule 65 ter, the Pre-Trial Judge may be assisted in the performance of his duties by one of the Senior Legal Officers assigned to the Chambers. Unfortunately, she is not with us today but I would like her to recommend to arrange a conference with the parties in order to discuss matters relating to the preparation of trial and the establishment of a work plan for it, and the parties will be informed. And then I would like that conference to be held before the Status Conference which is to take place in 120 days' time from now. Unless there is anything, the proceeding is adjourned.
